review.finding: The real committed test-traceability.json's generated_at is a deterministic epoch placeholder (1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00), so production would render the nonsensical 'Not yet in the requirement manifest (generated 1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00) — it predates this file.'
review.suggestion: Drop the parenthetical entirely, collapsing the ternary to a single constant string and removing the untested branch.

review.finding: The unresolvedReason condition does not exclude index.truncated — a truncated-but-'ok' index can produce a false 'predates this file' claim for a file that simply fell past the manifest's entry cap, contradicting the TestRow doc comment's own stated invariant.
review.suggestion: Add `&& !index.truncated` to the guard; extend the PARTIAL-manifest test with an assertion that the added row's unresolvedReason is null.

review.finding: Bumping `current` on an already-grandfathered entry in the same commit that grows the file is arguably the exact anti-ratchet contract violation the baseline exists to prevent, since anti_ratchet_check.py compares measured LOC directly against entry.current. The entry also lacked a `note` field, unlike the cited sibling precedent (server/scripts/regen-triage-fixtures.py, baseline lines 722-727).
review.suggestion: Either record a genuine bloat exception with an explanatory note matching the established grandfathered+adr+note convention, or split the mirror file to avoid growth.

review.finding: The new 'reads an ADDED file absent from an otherwise-OK manifest' test uses indexWith({}) which hardcodes generatedAt: null, so the toMatch(/predates this file/) assertion passed on both ternary branches — the generatedAt-bearing branch that actually ships in production had zero coverage, which is exactly why the HIGH epoch-placeholder finding went undetected.
review.suggestion: Closed by removing the generatedAt-bearing branch entirely per the HIGH finding above, rather than by adding a second fixture.

review.suggestion: Reword to describe the collector relationship without naming the deleted job.
